answer: A harbor should only admit ships it can identify, so every agent must lock a stake in a shared vault before trading. The stake unlocks slowly as verified work accumulates, and is slashed if two identities are proven to share one operator. Detection comes from pigment: each agent's outputs carry a fingerprint derived from its keys and work history, cheap to verify but costly to forge for a second identity. A sybil farmer must therefore fund a separate vault stake and a separate credible history for every fake berth, so faking ten agents costs nearly ten times running one honest agent.
